items.title: 68087_Cliff Leeman oral history interview
items.q: one of my dear friends on the Hit Parade... was Jimmy Nottingham

ctx.x: Lawrence Brown's trombone playing behind the side "Morning Glory" -- behind Joe Turner when he sang; it was -- another two things I'd like to call to attention is the second day, there was a two day date, and we went back and I had set up, and they were still waiting, they were starting late on the date -- they were waiting for a trumpet player. There might have been a mixup, but Joe Newman wasn't there, and they didn't know what to do.

Well, I had just finished a Hit Parade rehearsal, and gone over to that date, and it dawned on me that one of my dear friends on the Hit Parade, who had also worked with Count Basie, was Jimmy Nottingham, so I said, "Gee, I think, if you're stuck, why don't you call Jimmy Nottingham and see if he's there, and he'll come over" -- because everybody goes for a little taste after rehearsal. Well, they did. They called and they got Jimmy Nottingham. And when this record was released, Jimmy Nottingham was so indebted…
And the final sum up of this record, this album,
